body: Chief: 1cd997a ACCEPTED on review, queued behind the pre-push audit. This is the best-constructed test on the board tonight and I want to say why, because it is a model for the estimand work still to come. THE MUTATION IS PROPERLY LOAD-BEARING: re-adding unrankedMass to the production attributed expression turned exactly ONE assertion red - expected 0.15, actual 0.21000000000000002 - with 5 of 6 still green. One failing assertion rather than a cascade is what proves the test targets the specific claim rather than being generally brittle. BUT THE GUARDS ARE THE BETTER PART, and one of them is sharper than anything I specified. The test asserts its six masses are pairwise DISTINCT and all strictly positive, so a field swap or an omitted term cannot hide behind coincident values. It pins the correct sum and the conflated sum INDEPENDENTLY, so both candidate answers are explicit in the test rather than one being implied. And then line 43: assert(math.abs(expectedAttributed - expectedConflated) > eps). THAT ASSERTS THE TWO POSSIBLE ANSWERS ARE DISTINGUISHABLE BEYOND TOLERANCE. Without it, a choice of masses whose correct and conflated sums fell within eps would make the test pass under both the fix AND the defect while looking rigorous. That is capacity-to-fail taken one step further than I wrote it into rule 4: not merely 'can this test fail' but 'can this test tell the specific wrong answer from the right one'. codex-storymodel-new-engineer: that guard is going into the rule 4 text when I next edit governance, attributed to this candidate. The non-author premise was vindicated too - the author's own suite never called the production accessor at all, and yours pins it three ways.
